title: Compatible bounded-above resolutions from a quotient-generating class
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal A$ containing every zero object, stable under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, and such that every object $M$ admits an epimorphism $P\to M$ with $P\in\mathcal P$. Let $K$ be a $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define the good truncation $T_n=\tau_{\le n}K$ by $T_n^i=K^i$ for $i<n$, $T_n^n=\ker(d_K^n)$, and $T_n^i=0$ for $i>n$, with the differentials induced from $K$; write $j_n:T_n\to T_{n+1}$ for the canonical inclusion. There exist complexes $E_n$, morphisms $u_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ and termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphisms $e_n:E_n\to T_n$, for all integers $n\ge1$, such that $e_{n+1}\circ u_n=j_n\circ e_n$ as morphisms of complexes. Each $E_n$ is bounded above (there is an integer $b_n$ with $E_n^i=0$ for $i>b_n$) and every term $E_n^i$ lies in $\mathcal P$. Moreover each $u_n^i$ is a split monomorphism and its cokernel lies in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system (statement and proof, including the strictification of the homotopy square and final epicification).

proof.text: For each n, the good truncation T_n is strictly zero above n. Apply the bounded-above subcategory left resolution theorem to obtain a termwise epic quasi-isomorphism with terms in P. In particular this supplies the initial stage at n=1.

source.place: Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system, induction and final contractible-disk addition

proof.text: Given a bounded-above P-complex E and its augmentation e to T_n, form f=e followed by the canonical map to T_(n+1). The cone has terms E^(i+1) plus T_(n+1)^i, so max(b,n+1) bounds it. Resolve the cone using the same subcategory left resolution theorem, obtaining r:Q→Cone(f).

source.place: Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system, induction and final contractible-disk addition

proof.text: Use the explicit coordinate construction of RelativeBiprodConeExtension, retaining that the term isomorphism carries the inclusion to the first biproduct injection. Write r=(a,b). Its component equations give the twisted differential (d_E,-a;0,d_Q) on E^i plus Q^i and the chain map g=(f,b) to T_(n+1). The inclusion t satisfies t≫g=f strictly. Permuting the three summands gives Cone(g)≅Cone(r). Since r is a quasi-isomorphism its cone is acyclic, hence g is a quasi-isomorphism by the acyclic-cone criterion. The maximum of the bounds bounds the twisted complex.

source.place: Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system, induction and final contractible-disk addition

proof.text: For a bound N on T_(n+1), choose covers P_i→T_(n+1)^i for i≤N and put P_i=0 above N. Define the identity-disk complex D^i=P_i plus P_(i-1), with differential from the first summand to the second in the following degree. The covers and their composites with the target differential give a chain map a:D→T_(n+1) which is epic in every degree. The reverse second-to-first maps contract D. Thus adding D to the twisted complex gives a homotopy-equivalent bounded-above P-complex, a termwise epic augmentation, and the same strict square. This applies disks in every degree, so no separate argument about surjectivity in the last two degrees is needed.

source.place: Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system, induction and final contractible-disk addition

proof.text: Associate the term biproducts so that the final transition is the first injection E^i→E^i plus (Q^i plus D^i). It is split by the first projection. Transporting cokernels through this isomorphism identifies its cokernel with Q^i plus D^i. Finite-biproduct and isomorphism closure give all required class membership assertions.

source.place: Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system, induction and final contractible-disk addition

proof.text: Use Int.leInduction starting at 1, storing each complex, its augmentation and the four stage properties. Choose the next stage by the preceding construction and the transition from its witness. The induction successor equation yields the strictly compatible transitions, splitness and cokernel membership. For indices below 1 use an arbitrary individual bounded-above resolution and zero transitions; the theorem imposes no conditions on these transitions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q107-c027378c9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks derived.tex at Tag 06XX (lemma-special-direct-system, lines 9213-9325, statement and full proof), Tag 05T7(1) (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, 5301-5360) and Tag 0G6C (lemma-improve-distinguished-triangle-homotopy, 3458-3484). The item agrees with 06XX hypothesis by hypothesis. The one extra hypothesis, that P is stable under isomorphisms, is the convention that makes 'cokernel lies in P' meaningful, and the only user (the parent lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence) applies the item to flat objects, which are stable under isomorphisms. I checked all eight steps. Steps 1-3: the cone C^i = T_{n+1}^i + E_n^{i+1} is bounded above and 05T7(1) applies. Step 4: I recomputed the signs; B = C(c)[-1] has differential with components (d_E,0) and (-c,d_Q), and the two backward rotations give (E_n,B,Q,-i[-1],p[-1],c), split with cokernel Q^i, as in 0G6C. Step 5: TR3 on the twice-rotated triangles uses the square dq = 1c, which holds by definition of c; after exact localization lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso (Mathlib isIso2_of_isIso13) makes L[f] invertible, and H^i factors through Q. Step 6: the corrected map f~ = f - (dH + Hd) with H = h r satisfies f~ u = a strictly, since r u = 1 and d_B u = u d_E; it is homotopic to f, so still a quasi-isomorphism, and it is epic below degree n. Step 7: the disk map g is a chain map, the image of g^{n+1} is im d_K^n, and surjectivity of H^{n+1}(f) covers degree n+1. Step 8: D is acyclic, e_{n+1} u_n = j_n e_n strictly, the terms and cokernels lie in P by finite biproducts, and the bound is max(b, n+1). The new node lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution is exactly 05T7(1). It is statement-only and self-contained, strictly smaller than the item, and passes small-case checks (K = 0, K = M[0]). Duplicate search: grep of the DAG for 05T7, 06XX and key words found only module-sheaf or flat specializations (lem-pc-flat-truncation-tower, lem-pc-flat-truncation-successor, lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement, lem-kun-bounded-flat-replacement), the dual 05T6 nodes and functorial-tower nodes; none is a duplicate. lean.statement: theorem subcategory_truncation_resolution_system {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (P : C → Prop) (hzero : ∀ X : C, IsZero X → P X) (hiso : ∀ {X : C} {Y : C}, CategoryTheory.Iso X Y → P X → P Y) (hbiprod : ∀ {X : C} {Y : C}, P X → P Y → P (X ⊞ Y)) (hcover : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (p : Y ⟶ X), P Y ∧ Epi p) (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) : ∃ (E : ℤ → CochainComplex C ℤ) (e : ∀ n : ℤ, E n ⟶ K.truncLE n) (u : ∀ n : ℤ, E n ⟶ E (n + 1)), (∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ n → u n ≫ e (n + 1) = e n ≫ subcategoryTruncationMap K n) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ n → (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, P ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Epi ((e n).f i)) ∧ QuasiIso (e n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ n → (∀ i : ℤ, IsSplitMono ((u n).f i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, P (cokernel ((u n).f i))))
